title: Acknowledgements
html:
Much of what I know about production systems came from working through problems with other engineers.

I am grateful to the colleagues who took the time to explain unfamiliar systems, challenge my assumptions, investigate production failures with me, or share ideas that changed how I approached a problem. Some of the lessons in this book began during incidents. Often, the deeper understanding came afterward, when we returned to the evidence, examined what we had missed, and discussed what we could have done differently.

I am also grateful to the engineers who share their experiences publicly. Postmortems, technical articles, conference talks, and open-source projects have allowed me to learn from systems and failures far beyond those I have encountered in my own career. I have particularly appreciated the engineers who document difficult decisions, acknowledge mistakes, and explain what they learned along the way.

My thanks go to the mentors, managers, and teammates who trusted me with responsibilities I was still learning to handle. Their guidance, patience, and willingness to share their knowledge have contributed greatly to my growth as an engineer.

To my family and friends, thank you for your patience, encouragement, and understanding throughout the writing of this book. Many evenings and weekends went into these chapters, often at the expense of time we could have spent together. Your support made it possible for me to see this project through.

And to you, the reader, thank you for giving this book your time. I hope something in these chapters helps you understand a difficult production failure, recognize an assumption worth questioning, or approach an unfamiliar engineering problem with greater confidence.

Any errors are mine.
